title: Visual world for the Nitaq CRM redesign
question: The roll assigned Sharjah Grid. Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or ask for the category standard.

options.label: Sharjah Grid
options.lineage: Islamic 8-fold geometric construction · Sharjah's own architectural language
options.thesis: An interface constructed like Islamic geometry: one strict proportional grid rules every screen, so precision itself becomes the brand.
options.viewport: A calm stone-white workspace ruled by hairlines and an 8pt rhythm; a khatam-star product mark; emerald owns primary actions and live states; totals set like a ledger with tabular numerals; Arabic-ready dual-script type.
options.risk: If the geometry turns decorative — patterns scattered as ornament — it tips into theme-park; the geometry must stay structural (grid, proportion, one constructed mark) or it fails.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.lineage: stagecraft theater lighting — night-to-day cyc wall
options.thesis: The workspace as a lit stage: content held in horizon bands that pass from night into day.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dark atmospheric bands fight dense bilingual tables and bright Sharjah office use.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.lineage: textile drape — one cord transforms flat cloth into volume
options.thesis: Screens as flat planes that gather into shaped volumes on command.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a single-object transformation grammar has nowhere to live across 27 CRUD modules.

options.label: Night Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm luminous gauges that agree with each other; the practiced eye sweeps them.
options.case: Partial fit for a finance dashboard, but dial grammar obscures tables and reads gimmicky at CRM scale.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The clean neutral SaaS admin — Linear/Stripe grammar played straight, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White ground, grayscale hierarchy, one green accent, refined sidebar and data tables at full craft.
